topic: Someone finds a time capsule they don't remember burying
text: I dug, claws scraping at the earth. It wasn't my usual search for roots or grubs, soft things to quiet the gnaw inside. This was deeper, harder. My nose twitched, catching a scent, old and faint, like buried secrets. The soil gave way, and there it was, not food, not prey, but something foreign, cold. I bared my teeth at the intrusion, the dared disturbance. Who leaves such things? Who dares mark this earth, this hunting ground, with their forgotten stains? My hackles rose, the fur on my back pricking the air. I sniffed again, more scents layered, too many, too recent. This place, these marks—they're mine, by right, by claw. I growled, a low warning, a promise of chase, of fight. They will not go unchallenged, these silent trespassers. Not while my paws can dig, not while my voice can roar.
